Mutations in GNAS, GNAS-AS1, or STX16 (all implicated in Pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1B) can lead to haploinsufficiency affecting cAMP-mediated signaling. This dysregulation of cAMP signaling downstream of GNAS leads to phenotypes common to both diseases, such as short stature and obesity. While MONDO:0014074 does not have a specific GNAS mutation profile defined, the shared HPO terms suggest a convergence on the cAMP signaling pathway.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of mutations in GNAS, GNAS-AS1, or STX16 in individuals with MONDO:0014074 and pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1B, or if the identified mutations do not demonstrably impair cAMP signaling. _(variant: The presence of common variants (AF > 1%) in GNAS, GNAS-AS1, or STX16 in the general population that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on GNAS-mediated cAMP signaling provides a potential therapeutic target for both disorders. Modulating this pathway could offer a unified approach to treating some of the core manifestations of both MONDO:0014074 and pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1B.
